data.title: Disruption of the p70(s6k)/p85(s6k) gene reveals a small mouse phenotype and a new functional S6 kinase
data.authors: Shima H; Pende M; Chen Y; Fumagalli S; Thomas G; Kozma SC

evidence.label: Animal model
evidence.note: this describes the kind of study, not its quality

data.model_system: p70/p85 S6K1 knockout mice; embryonic fibroblasts and liver from knockout mice; S6K2 cloning and kinase assays
data.finding: Mice with the S6K1 gene disrupted were viable and fertile but smaller, with the growth effect strongest during embryonic development. Unexpectedly, ribosomal protein S6 was still phosphorylated normally after mitogen stimulation in knockout liver and fibroblasts, and in knockout fibroblasts S6 phosphorylation and the rise in 5'TOP mRNA translation were as sensitive to rapamycin as in wild-type cells. A database search identified a second S6 kinase, S6K2, which had mitogen-dependent and rapamycin-sensitive S6 kinase activity and was up-regulated in all tissues of the knockout mice examined, most of all in thymus. S6K2 can therefore partly compensate for loss of S6K1. Boundary: Mouse knockout and mouse cells. Body size and S6 signalling only; the 5'TOP result means S6K1 alone is not required in these cells, not that S6 kinases are irrelevant. Drafted from the abstract only.
data.abstract_excerpt: Recent studies have shown that the p70(s6k)/p85(s6k) signaling pathway plays a critical role in cell growth by modulating the translation of a family of mRNAs termed 5'TOPs, which encode components of the protein synthetic apparatus. Here we demonstrate that homozygous disruption of the p70(s6k)/p85(s6k) gene does not affect viability or fertility of mice, but that it has a significant effect on animal growth, especially during embryogenesis. Surprisingly, S6 phosphorylation in liver or in fibroblasts from p70(s6k)/p85(s6k)-deficient mice proceeds normally in response to mitogen stimulation.

extracted_findings.intervention: Germline S6K1 (p70/p85 S6K) knockout; rapamycin in knockout fibroblasts
extracted_findings.target: Body size; S6 phosphorylation; 5'TOP mRNA translation; S6K2 expression
extracted_findings.effect: Loss of S6K1 reduces body size, especially embryonic growth, while S6 phosphorylation and rapamycin-sensitive 5'TOP translation persist via S6K2
